gap: No result ChatGPT got says which of its suggested power banks can actually give a Samsung Galaxy its 45 W fast charge (Samsung's 'Super Fast Charging 2.0', which needs a charging mode called PPS). Anker Prime A110A, AOHi Starship 240W and Anker Zolo 165W (A1695) can. The original UGREEN 145W 25,000 mAh (PB205) has no PPS and charged Samsung phones at no more than 14 W in Techtest's review.
standout_why: Popular Science (cited in five of the seven chats) never mentions PPS, Samsung Super Fast Charging or 45 W; on cables it only says to use a 100 W cable for the UGREEN 130W. It does flag that the UGREEN 145W is labelled 145W but rated 140/65/22.5 W by port, but not that an older version (PB205) lacks PPS and tops out at 100 W from one port. Wirecutter (through the proxy result, cited twice) covers 140 W per port, the included 240 W cable and the 100 Wh airline limit, but says nothing about PPS or Samsung 45 W, and nothing about Samsung on the Anker Prime beyond 'most handheld devices'. Wired could not be fetched. Every ChatGPT answer lists 'Samsung Galaxy: 45W with compatible PPS support' in its table but never says which of its own cards have that support, and one chat put the UGREEN 145W forward as its 'best value'.
decides: For a Samsung Galaxy owner (the shopper type ChatGPT asks about first), the Anker Prime A110A and AOHi Starship 240W both meet the requirement. Anker Prime offers 4.5–21 V at up to 5 A (Techtest) and AOHi offers 3.3–21 V/5 A (ChargerLAB). That covers the S25+/Ultra, which charges at 15 V × 3 A (SamMobile), and the older 45 W models, which charge at 10 V × 4.5 A and need a 5 A cable. That supports keeping both picks. It also means a UGREEN '145W' listing should not be recommended to Samsung buyers unless it is clearly the newer 140 W-per-port version: Techtest found the 2023 PB205 has no PPS, no 28 V level, a 100 W maximum from one port and 14 W into Samsung phones. A MacBook Pro 16 M4 Pro drew 133.47 W from the AOHi on Apple's MagSafe 3 cable (ChargerLAB), which confirms its 140 W claim works with a real MacBook.
